Examples: The court upheld the original decision. | Officials are sworn to uphold the constitution.

Pattern: intervene; intervene in + N
Examples: Ministers intervened only when the story broke. | The regulator intervened in two takeovers.

Pattern: decentralise + N; thường bị động
Examples: Planning was decentralised to the districts. | They decentralised the staff and centralised the decisions.

Pattern: centralise + N; thường bị động
Examples: Procurement was centralised to save money. | Centralising the service closed nine local offices.

Pattern: mobilise + N
Examples: The campaign mobilised nine thousand volunteers. | They mobilised the membership within a weekend.

Definition: chấp nhận thất bại hoặc nhượng bộ
Pattern: concede + N; concede that + clause
Examples: She conceded within an hour of the count. | The minister conceded two of the four points.

Pattern: rig + N (an election, a ballot)
Examples: The ballot was rigged in nine polling stations. | They rigged the selection and lost the seat anyway.

Pattern: pledge + N; pledge to + V
Examples: Both parties pledged to protect the allowance. | They pledged nine million and delivered three.

Pattern: consult + sb + on/about + N
Examples: Nobody consulted the tenants on the demolition. | They consulted the trade before the inspectors.

Definition: thôi giữ chức, không tái tranh cử
Pattern: stand down; stand down as + N
Examples: She stood down after four terms. | He stood down as leader but kept his seat.

Pattern: run for + N (office, mayor)
Examples: She ran for mayor and lost by nine votes. | He ran for office twice before winning.

Pattern: come to power; come to power in + năm
Examples: The coalition came to power in 2017. | They came to power promising to abolish the charge.

Pattern: take office; take office as + N
Examples: She took office in the middle of the strike. | He took office as mayor the following Monday.

Pattern: push through + N hoặc push + N + through; tách được
Examples: They pushed the bill through in a single night. | The reform was pushed through without consultation.

Pattern: water down + N hoặc water + N + down; tách được
Examples: The clause was watered down in committee. | They watered the targets down to nothing.

Pattern: back down; back down over + N
Examples: The minister backed down over the fee. | Neither side would back down for a fortnight.

Definition: xin rút, không tham gia (chương trình, thoả thuận)
Pattern: opt out of + N
Examples: Two councils opted out of the scheme. | Schools were allowed to opt out entirely.

Definition: là thành viên (hội đồng, uỷ ban)
Pattern: sit on + N (a committee, a board)
Examples: She sits on three committees and chairs none. | He sat on the board for eleven years.

Pattern: stand for + N (election, parliament)
Examples: He stood for parliament at twenty-four. | She stood for election in a ward she had never visited.

Pattern: rule out + N hoặc rule + N + out; tách được
Examples: Ministers ruled out any new charge. | They ruled the option out before the consultation closed.

Definition: dời lên sớm hơn; đưa ra
Pattern: bring forward + N hoặc bring + N + forward; tách được
Examples: The vote was brought forward by a week. | They brought the legislation forward after the fire.

Pattern: step aside; step aside for + sb
Examples: He stepped aside for a younger candidate. | She stepped aside rather than split the party.

Pattern: win over + sb hoặc win + sb + over; tách được
Examples: The plan won over the sceptics in the end. | She won the committee over with one table of figures.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; the + shadow cabinet + responds
Examples: The shadow cabinet published its own costings. | Three members of the shadow cabinet resigned together.

Definition: người đốc thúc kỉ luật đảng
Pattern: danh từ đếm được; the + party whip + instructs
Examples: The party whip told members to support the bill. | She defied the party whip twice in one session.

Pattern: danh từ không đếm được; collective + ministerial responsibility
Examples: Collective ministerial responsibility used to mean resignation. | Nobody accepted ministerial responsibility for the loss.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; have/breach + a statutory duty
Examples: Councils have a statutory duty to house the homeless. | The authority breached its statutory duty for two years.

Definition: quy định của chính quyền địa phương
Pattern: danh từ đếm được; pass/enforce + a local byelaw
Examples: A local byelaw bans drinking in the square. | The local byelaw was never enforced after 1998.

Pattern: danh từ đếm được; serve/a four-year + term of office
Examples: She served two terms of office as mayor. | The term of office was shortened to four years.

Definition: làm theo chủ trương của đảng
Pattern: toe the party line
Examples: Most members toed the party line and said nothing. | He refused to toe the party line on the closure.

Pattern: be/remain + in office
Examples: They were in office for eleven years. | She remained in office through two scandals.

Definition: trong phòng kín, không công khai
Pattern: be decided/meet + behind closed doors
Examples: The deal was agreed behind closed doors. | Committees that meet behind closed doors invite suspicion.

Definition: vấn đề chính trị gai góc
Pattern: be/become + a political hot potato
Examples: Rural bus funding became a political hot potato. | The site is a political hot potato nobody will touch.

Pattern: cross the floor + to + N
Examples: Two members crossed the floor that session. | He crossed the floor and lost the next election.

Pattern: hold/inherit + a safe seat
Examples: She inherited a safe seat and never canvassed again. | A safe seat makes a lazy representative.

Pattern: in/walk + the corridors of power
Examples: Decisions are made in the corridors of power, not the chamber. | He spent thirty years in the corridors of power.

Pattern: make/perform + a u-turn + on + N
Examples: The government made a u-turn on the charge within a week. | A u-turn is cheaper than a bad policy.

Pattern: be/live + in the public eye
Examples: Ministers live in the public eye and complain about it. | The inquiry put the department in the public eye.

Pattern: pass the buck + to + N
Examples: Each department passed the buck to the next. | Nobody could pass the buck once the minutes were published.
